claims_about_writeup.quote: submission/contribution.md — the method, mechanism, and what's new vs. the white-bear paper (honest about the shared mechanism; the construction and the WM-load control are mine).
claims_about_writeup.why: The write-up does describe the method, invoke the white-bear paper as the mechanism's origin, and attribute the self-authored contrast and the WM-load control (arbitrary-number control) to the author's own construction, matching this description.

message_source_quote: The key unlock was a paper in `papers/` — *White-Bear Steering* (Raman et al. 2026) — which is literally the same setup (Qwen3.5-4B, association, plain J-lens at 26/28/30) and identifies the mechanism: a **concept-agnostic "stance" direction, injected at layers 20–24 (below the read band) with a large, narrow dose**, makes the layers above (25–29) keep developing the implied concept instead of dropping it for next-token prediction.
writeup_source_quote: The starting point is the stance-steering observation in Orrery Lab's white-bear paper (`papers/`): a direction extracted from "think about X / don't think about X while copying" pairs, injected at a mid-depth band with an unusually large dose, makes implied concepts readable to the unchanged J-lens.

differences.what: Additional ablations (content/task/sequentiality and family-contrast directions failing, and centring-style baselines capping at 0.15) cited as further evidence isolating the novel 'active ingredient' relative to the source
differences.message_quote: Content/task/sequentiality and family-contrast directions all failed destructively, confirming the stance is the narrow working ingredient.

differences.what: Citation precision: message supplies explicit author/year attribution for the source, which the write-up only names informally

rationale: Both documents credit the same source (the white-bear/Orrery Lab paper on stance steering) as the origin of the mechanism the method builds on, and both frame the novelty identically: a self-authored, benchmark-free hold/expel contrast plus a semantic-vs-generic-working-memory-load control that isolates the 'active ingredient,' while conceding the underlying mechanism is shared rather than fundamentally new. The message adds a few extra supporting details (more precise citation, additional failed ablation variants) not present in the write-up, but makes no false claims about what the write-up contains and no material change to the overlap/novelty story.
